However, the emotion-regulation instructions implemented only down-regulation (distancing) of emotions and did not include explicit up-regulation trials or instructions; thus it does not meet I6 (requires up- and down-regulation). In addition, the healthy control sample is mixed adolescent and adult (ages 12.1–29.5) rather than clearly a sample of healthy adults only, so it does not strictly meet I7. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related, task-based fMRI study that explicitly implements emotion regulation instructions (reappraise to decrease negative emotion and an ‘increase’ condition to up-regulate negative emotion) and reports within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > attend negative, suppress > attend negative). The paper includes a screened healthy control group (HC) and performs second-level, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (main task effects, between-group contrasts, and whole-brain regression analyses) with cluster-level FWE correction; results are reported in the main text and supplementary materials. Although stimuli were negative and neutral (no positive stimuli), the task includes both up- and down-regulation goals, which meets the intent of the inclusion criterion regarding regulation direction. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of reappraisal that reports within-task contrast ("decrease" negative vs "look" negative) and voxel-wise whole-brain analyses, but it does not include a healthy adult sample performing reappraisal and does not assess reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions or both up- and down-regulation. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis.

This study is a resting-state fMRI study using stochastic dynamic causal modeling (effective connectivity/DCM) in PTSD, PTSD+DS, and healthy controls. It does include a healthy control group (n=52) meeting I7. However, it is not a task-based fMRI study and does not report any task activation contrasts of emotion regulation or reappraisal (I5, I6, I8 not met). It provides no whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or task-based group-level contrasts (I9/I10 not met). Moreover, it reports only resting-state effective connectivity analyses (DCM), which meets exclusion criterion E5 (studies that report only effective connectivity/resting-state analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on task-based emotion-regulation fMRI.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive reappraisal in healthy adults and reports within-task reappraisal contrasts and whole-brain group-level analyses (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10). However, it only examines down-regulation of negative emotions (decrease-negative vs. look-negative) and does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or up-regulation conditions. Therefore it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I6, which requires reappraisal of positive and negative emotions using up- and down-regulation. No exclusion criteria were met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive emotion regulation using situation-focused cognitive reappraisal with explicit up-regulation and down-regulation instructions (day 1) and re-exposure (day 2). It tests within-task contrasts (e.g., down-regulation > look aversive; up-regulation > look aversive; distraction contrasts) at the group level and reports both ROI and exploratory whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected thresholds and supplementary tables/coordinates). The sample is healthy adults with exclusion of neurological/psychiatric disorders. Reporting includes group-level whole-brain results and coordinate tables/figures. All required inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is a task-based fMRI study in a healthy adult sample that reports a within-task contrast (affect labeling > gender labeling) from a group-level whole-brain analysis (with peak coordinates) and provides full methods/results, it does NOT use a reappraisal task. Inclusion criterion I6 specifically requires use of reappraisal (up- or down-regulation) as the emotion regulation strategy. This study investigates affect labeling (implicit emotion regulation), not explicit reappraisal, so I6 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that uses cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise > Look-Neutral) to down-regulate negative emotion, includes a healthy control group, and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with corrected clusters (coordinates and figures) for the relevant contrasts. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal as emotion regulation — down-regulation of negative emotion), I7 (contains a healthy adult control group), I8 (reports within-task contrasts related to regulation, e.g., Reappraise > Look-Neutral), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported and corrected), and I10 (results reported as tables/figures/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6. Although it is a task-based fMRI reappraisal study, the paradigm tests only distancing (down-regulation) of negative stimuli and does not include reappraisal of positive stimuli or up-regulation conditions required by I6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (includes a healthy control group with no psychiatric/neurological disorders), I8 (reports within-task emotion-regulation contrasts such as “distance > baseline” and reappraisal success), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported using SnPM with FWE correction), and I10 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates and figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Confidence: 0.85.

The full text is a task-based fMRI study that examines cognitive reappraisal of negative IAPS images (down-regulation). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult samples with no Axis I disorder), I8 (reports within-task contrast Reappraise Negative > Attend Negative), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I10 (whole-brain results reported with tables/coordinates). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 — the task involves only reappraisal of negative emotions (down-regulation) and does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or both up- and down-regulation goals as required. Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I6.

The full text is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (distancing) with whole-brain group analyses in a healthy developmental sample (ages 6–23). It reports reappraisal-related within-task contrasts (e.g., Reappraisal/Negative > Reactivity/Negative) with voxelwise maps and coordinate tables and includes adult participants with no reported disorders. However, the study only examines negative and neutral stimuli and implements a down-regulation (distancing) strategy; it does not include reappraisal of positive stimuli nor explicit up-regulation trials. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 (requires reappraisal of positive and negative emotions and use of up- and down-regulation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Consequently, the study is excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review's target-sample and task-valence/regulation criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study using an emotion regulation task), I8 (reports a within-task emotion-regulation contrast: Reappraise > Maintain), I9 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain regression analyses within an a priori emotion-regulation mask), and I10 (whole-brain results are clearly described and plotted). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (the task involves only down-regulation of negative stimuli via reappraisal; it does not include reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions nor explicit up- and down-regulation conditions), and I7 (the sample is clinical patients with anxiety/depression; there is no group of healthy adults with no psychiatric/medical history). Exclusion criteria applied: none (no E3–E6 violations). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Given the review requires healthy adult target samples and reappraisal of positive/negative with up/down regulation, the paper must be excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal task (reappraise vs look-negative; look-negative vs reappraise) focused on emotion regulation. The sample includes a healthy control group with no psychiatric history. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation for the healthy/control sample (reappraise>look-negative; look-negative>reappraise) and describes voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses (with whole-brain corrected within-group maps and voxelwise between-group tests), with results presented in text/figures. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets the review objective and inclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study (engagement vs distraction) including healthy non-offender controls and reports within-task regulation contrasts and whole-brain group-level analyses. However, the study’s regulation strategy is distraction (attentional distraction) rather than cognitive reappraisal (up- or down-regulation via reappraisal), so it fails to meet I6 (reappraisal-specific task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded because it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I6.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive reappraisal and includes healthy control participants, reports a within-task emotion-regulation contrast (‘regulate’ > ‘experience’), and performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates reported. However, the fMRI task only involves down-regulation of negative emotions (reappraising negative IAPS images) and does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or explicit up-regulation conditions. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (task includes reappraisal of positive and negative emotions and both up- and down-regulation goals) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal that explicitly implements up- and down-regulation of emotional valence using IAPS stimuli and title-based reinterpretation. Participants were healthy adult university students with no reported psychiatric or neurological disorders. The fMRI analysis modeled IAPS2–IAPS1 (after vs before reappraisal) contrasts at the first level and conducted group-level, voxelwise second-level tests (independent-samples t tests) comparing activity during up- and down-regulation; results are reported in tables/figures (Table 2, Fig. 2) and supplementary material signaled for task activations, satisfying whole-brain reporting. No exclusion criteria (ROIs-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or only between-group-without-within-task maps) are met based on the full text. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI reappraisal studies.

Exclusion criteria met: E4 (study reports ROI-based analyses using AAL masks and presents ROI beta weights/ROC analyses without reporting a group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study with implicit and explicit emotion regulation tasks) and I8 (reports within-task emotion-regulation contrast Reappraise > Maintain). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (does not include reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions nor both up- and down-regulation; only down-regulation of negative images), I7 (target sample is clinical: patients with social anxiety disorder; no healthy adult group), I9 (no group-level whole-brain/voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it violates E4 and fails to meet required I6, I7, and I9.

This is a task-based 3T fMRI study in healthy adults that reports a within-task, group-level whole-brain contrast (NNEG-DESC > NEG-DESC) and presents coordinate tables/figures. However, the experimental task only uses negative affective images and an implicit (incidental) down-regulation manipulation (non-negative vs negative preceding descriptions). It does not include reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions nor explicit up- and down-regulation goals across valence. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI study using the SEAT task in an fMRI scanner), I7 (sample: healthy adults screened for psychiatric/medical conditions), I8 (reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation-like processes: like/dislike > male/female [appraisal] and indoor/outdoor > male/female [attention shift]), I9 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported using FWE-corrected thresholds), I10 (whole-brain results presented in text/tables/figures). Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (study does NOT investigate reappraisal as an explicit emotion regulation strategy involving up- and down-regulation goals; instead it examines implicit attention shifting and an appraisal/labeling like/dislike task rather than instructed reappraisal). Because I6 is required and is not satisfied, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that implemented cognitive reappraisal with explicit up-regulation (Increase) and down-regulation (Decrease) instructions using emotional (aversive) images. Participants were healthy adults with no history of neurological or psychiatric disease (n=23). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (e.g., Increase > Look-Negative; Decrease > Look-Negative) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with FWE cluster correction; results are described in the text and illustrated (coordinates/thresholds provided). Although stimuli were aversive (negative) images, the task explicitly tests both up- and down-regulation goals, satisfying the reappraisal/up-down criterion as intended. The study additionally reports ROI and PPI connectivity analyses but also provides whole-brain activation maps and contrasts. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the paper reports only ROI/small-volume-corrected analyses for the emotion-regulation contrasts (amygdala PSC/SVC) rather than group-level whole-brain task activation maps for the regulation contrasts, meeting exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), and I8 (within-task regulation contrasts reported: reappraisal > watch and suppression > watch). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (the task uses reappraisal/suppression of negative emotions only; it does not include reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions nor both up- and down-regulation goals), and I9 (the target emotion-regulation analyses are not reported as group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps; regulation results are reported via ROI/SVC and extracted PSC). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED (E4).

This study is a resting-state fMRI investigation of cortico-limbic connectivity under acute tryptophan depletion and MAOA genotype; it does not involve any task-based emotion regulation paradigm (reappraisal). Exclusion ID met: E5 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (sample: healthy adults with no reported neurological/psychiatric disorders). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (does not use reappraisal up/down regulation of emotions), I8 (no within-task emotion-regulation contrasts reported), I9 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion present). Therefore the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis of task-based reappraisal fMRI studies.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) of cognitive emotion regulation in healthy adult participants (I7) that reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., CER>NoCER) (I8) and uses group-level contrasts to define regions (consistent with whole-brain voxelwise analysis) (I9). However, it does not meet I6: the task implements cognitive self-distancing to down-regulate negative emotional responses to aversive images only; it does not report reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions nor both up- and down-regulation goals as required by I6. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I6.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive reappraisal and reports within-task contrasts (e.g., AR > AM) and group-level whole-brain analyses (meets I5, I8, I9, I10). However, it does not report reappraisal of positive emotions or explicit up-regulation of positive affect; the task uses aversive (negative) and neutral images and primarily implements down-regulation of negative emotion (fails I6). Additionally, it is unclear whether the low-EXT group can be confirmed as a healthy adult group with no prior neurological, medical, or psychiatric disorders (I7 not explicitly demonstrated in the text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met. Therefore the study is excluded because I6 is not satisfied and I7 is not clearly met.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: the fMRI emotion-regulation task uses distraction (memorize vs. view) rather than reappraisal with explicit up- and down-regulation of positive/negative emotions required by the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (includes a healthy control group), I8 (reports within-task emotion-regulation contrasts such as MEMORIZE vs VIEW and NEGATIVE vs NEUTRAL), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I10 (results reported with peak coordinates and figures/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (reappraisal task requirement). No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E6) directly apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly tests cognitive reappraisal (positive reappraisal and minimizing reappraisal) during an fMRI task. The sample consists of healthy adult participants screened for psychiatric disorders. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., positive reappraisal > natural response; minimizing reappraisal > natural response), group-level random-effects analyses, and whole-brain voxelwise results (cluster-corrected whole-brain contrasts and reported peak coordinates), as well as ROI/SVC follow-ups. Results include whole-brain parametric maps and coordinates for relevant contrasts (ventral striatum, vmPFC, etc.). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, not only between-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of reappraisal during laughter perception and includes healthy control participants, but it does NOT meet the review’s specific reappraisal criterion (I6). Specifically: Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study), I7 (includes a healthy control group with no psychiatric disorders), I8 (reports within-task contrast REAPPRAISAL > NO REAPPRAISAL), I9 (conducted group-level whole-brain analyses, in addition to ROI), I10 (whole-brain results and ROI results clearly described). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (requires reappraisal of positive and negative emotions using both up- and down-regulation goals; this study uses a single reappraisal manipulation aimed at reducing negative interpretation of social threat and does not include explicit up-regulation or both valences). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3/E4/E5/E6 do not apply). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Because I6 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded per the review rules.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E4 — the paper reports ROI-based amygdala analyses and does not present group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study), I7 (healthy adult sample with no reported neurological/psychiatric disorders), I8 (reports within-task contrast related to emotion regulation: contrast between threat-watching with suppression priming vs without). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (study examines expressive suppression, not reappraisal as required by I6), I9 (no whole-brain voxelwise results reported). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults that reports within-task contrasts for emotion regulation (Decrease > Maintain) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (satisfies I5, I7, I8, I9, I10). However, the focal inclusion criterion I6 requires studies of cognitive reappraisal as the emotion regulation strategy (up- and down-regulation using reappraisal). In this study participants were free to choose strategies and the vast majority (22/24) spontaneously used distraction; only 2 used reappraisal and those were not included in the analyzed sample (analyses were performed on the 18 subjects using distraction). Therefore the study does not meet I6 and must be excluded. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (reappraisal-specific task).

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal in combat-exposed veterans that reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (Reappraise > Maintain) and presents whole-brain tables; however it does NOT meet the review's requirement to include reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions and both up- and down-regulation goals. The study only employs reappraisal of negative images with down-regulation instruction. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (contains a control group of adults without PTSD), I8 (reports within-task Reappraise > Maintain contrasts), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I10 (whole-brain results provided in tables/figures). Exclusion criteria met: none ([])

This is a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation in healthy adults that reports within-task reappraisal contrasts (Reappraise > Maintain) and whole-brain cluster-corrected results. However, the ERT reappraisal task involves only down-regulation of negative IAPS images (decreasing negative affect) and does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or explicit up-regulation conditions. Therefore it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I6 (requires reappraisal of positive and negative emotions and up- and down-regulation goals). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that implemented cognitive reappraisal with explicit up-regulation (Increase) and down-regulation (Decrease) of emotions in response to angry faces. The sample consists of healthy adult participants with no reported neurological/psychiatric disorders. The paper reports within-task, group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Decrease > Observe-angry; Increase > Observe-angry) with cluster-level FWE correction and tables/figures of coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review and violates no exclusion criteria.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of reappraisal (I5) and it includes a healthy control group with no past/current psychiatric diagnoses (I7), it does not meet key inclusion requirements for the review. The task focusses on reappraisal of negative (vs neutral) pictures only and does not include reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions or up- and down-regulation goals as specified (I6 not met). Moreover, based on the provided full text, the reported results emphasize group × time interactions and patient-related contrasts; there is no clear reporting of a group-level, whole-brain task activation map (e.g., reappraise > maintain) for the healthy target sample in the text (I8 and I9 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly triggered by the provided content. Therefore the study must be excluded for not satisfying all inclusion criteria (notably I6, I8, I9).

This is a task-based fMRI study of reappraisal (distancing) with healthy adults and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain group-level results; however, the task only implements reappraisal of negative stimuli with down-regulation (RegulateNeg vs WatchNeg) and does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or up-regulation conditions. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 requiring reappraisal of positive and negative emotions using up- and down-regulation goals. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. No exclusion criteria were triggered (exclusion_criteria_applied = []). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete = false).

This is a task-based fMRI study that uses cognitive reappraisal (distancing) to down-regulate negative emotions (Social-Reg and Self-Reg). Participants were healthy adults (young females) with no reported neurological or psychiatric disorders. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (Social-Reg > Social-Look; Self-Reg > Self-Look) at the group level using whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses with cluster-wise FWE correction; coordinates and tables are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion applied: E4. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample screened for psychiatric/medical conditions), I8 (reports within-task contrasts related to reappraisal, e.g., Reappraise vs Maintain). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (task involves only down-regulation of negative emotions; no up-regulation or positive-emotion reappraisal reported), I9 (the reported significant results are from ROI/small-volume-corrected analyses rather than an accompanying whole-brain, voxelwise task-activation map for the target contrasts). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports within-task reappraisal contrasts and seed-based gPPI connectivity results, but it does not meet key inclusion criteria required by the review. Specifically, the task only involves reappraisal of negative (not positive) stimuli and primarily implements down-regulation, so it does not satisfy I6 (reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions and up- and down-regulation). Critically, the reported target analyses are seed-based PPI/gPPI connectivity and ROI-extracted coupling estimates rather than group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation maps; thus I9 is not met. Because the paper reports only ROI/seed-based connectivity (and references prior ROI results), it violates exclusion criteria E4 and E5. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), and I8 (reports a within-task reappraisal vs watch contrast used in analyses). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 and I9. Exclusion criteria met: E4 and E5. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that implemented cognitive reappraisal with explicit up- (Increase) and down-regulation (Decrease) goals while participants viewed emotional film clips. The sample consists of healthy adults with no reported neurological/psychiatric disorders. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (e.g., Increase + Decrease vs Look-Sports) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with tables and figures. Although the paper also includes effective connectivity (DCM) analyses, whole-brain task activation maps are reported, so exclusion for connectivity-only analyses does not apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study with healthy control participants and reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps (satisfies I5, I7, I9, I10), it does NOT employ an emotion-regulation reappraisal task nor report within-task reappraisal contrasts. The paradigm is a delayed working-memory task with negative emotional distractors and analyses focus on distractor effects (e.g., negative > scrambled) and effective connectivity (DCM). The study does not instruct up- or down-regulation (reappraisal) nor report contrasts such as “reappraise > look” or “down-regulate > maintain”. Therefore it fails to meet I6 (reappraisal task) and I8 (within-task emotion-regulation contrast) and must be excluded.

Exclusion E4 applies: the paper reports task-evoked activations using restricted masks/SVC (amygdala+insula, prefrontal masks, and masks derived from one-sample activations) rather than presenting an accompanying group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample with exclusion of psychiatric/medical disorders), I8 (reports within-task regulation contrast: Regulate > Maintain). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (task uses down-regulation of negative emotions only; no reappraisal of positive emotions or explicit up-regulation), I9 (no clear whole-brain group-level voxelwise activation map for the regulation contrast). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly investigates cognitive reappraisal with explicit up- (Increase) and down-regulation (Decrease) goals using film clips and IAPS pictures. Participants were healthy adults with no reported neurological/psychiatric disorders. The paper reports within-task contrasts (Increase>Look; Decrease>Look; Increase>Decrease) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8, FWE-corrected maps) with tables of coordinates and figures. Reporting satisfies whole-brain evidence requirements. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal that reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look-negative; look-negative > reappraise) in a screened healthy sample (ages 15–25). However, the fMRI task involves only down-regulation of negative social-affective images (reappraise vs look); it does not include reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions nor both up- and down-regulation goals as required by inclusion criterion I6. Therefore the study fails to meet I6 and must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy screened participants present), I8 (within-task reappraisal contrast reported), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I10 (results clearly described/tabled). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports within-task regulation contrasts and whole-brain group maps. However it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: the emotion regulation manipulation uses cognitive reappraisal (self-distancing) to down-regulate negative (aversive) images only — it does not include up-regulation conditions or reappraisal of positive emotions. Therefore I6 is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I8 (reports within-task regulation contrasts, e.g., Distance vs Attend), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are violated. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Given the single unmet inclusion criterion (I6), the study is excluded from this review.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that implements cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotion (Attend Negative vs Reappraise Negative). The sample consists of healthy young adults screened for psychiatric/medical exclusions. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (Reappraise Negative > Attend/Look Negative) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation results with cluster-level FWE correction, tables of coordinates, and figures. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study) and I7 (includes a healthy control group without psychiatric history). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (the task uses cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative stimuli only — it does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or explicit up-regulation conditions), I8 (the paper does not clearly report a within-task contrast (e.g., Reappraise > Maintain) as a group-level, whole-brain map specifically for the healthy control sample), and I9 (no clear group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map is reported for the target sample alone). Exclusion criterion met: E6 (effectively only between-group contrasts/interactions or combined-group task effects are presented for whole-brain results, with no standalone healthy-group whole-brain reappraisal map). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded.

Excluded because the study reports only ROI-restricted task analyses and does not provide a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I8 (reports a within-task reappraise>watch contrast). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (task includes reappraisal of negative stimuli only — no positive stimuli or explicit up-regulation trials), I9 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported; analyses are ROI-focused). Exclusion criterion met: E4 (only ROI analyses reported without an accompanying whole-brain map). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper must be excluded from the review.

This fMRI study is task-based, includes healthy control participants, reports within-task reappraisal contrasts (Reappraisal > Attend Negative) and whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates. However, the fMRI task only used negative (and neutral) stimuli and implemented reappraisal as down-regulation of negative affect; it did not include positive stimuli nor up-regulation goals. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (requires reappraisal of positive and negative emotions and up- and down-regulation goals). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of reappraisal in a healthy sample (ages 10.5–22.9) reporting within-task regulation contrasts and whole-brain group analyses; however it does not meet the review’s specific task requirement (I6). The paradigm uses distancing to down-regulate negative (aversive) stimuli and neutral stimuli; it does not include positive stimuli nor explicit up-regulation trials. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy participants including adults), I8 (reports within-task regulation contrasts, e.g., regulation vs reactivity), I9 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (requires reappraisal of positive and negative emotions and use of both up- and down-regulation goals). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to satisfy I6 while meeting the other criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal to downregulate negative emotion. Participants were healthy adults. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing reappraise versus look conditions during active regulation and long-term reexposure, and whole-brain GLM analyses with FWE thresholding and coordinate tables/figures. The methods, results, and discussion are fully present in the provided full text. Thus it satisfies the review’s criteria for inclusion as a task-based reappraisal fMRI study with group-level whole-brain results.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly implements an emotion regulation Reappraisal task (positive-emphasis reappraisal) and a Compassion up-regulation condition, with clear within-task contrasts (e.g., Reappraisal > Watch-Negative; Compassion > Watch-Negative; Compassion > Reappraisal). The sample comprises healthy adult long-term meditators with no reported neurological/psychiatric disorders. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results with cluster-level FWE correction and whole-brain contrasts reported in text/tables/figures. Therefore it meets all specified inclusion criteria and does not trigger any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study with healthy control participants and reports within-task contrasts and group-level voxelwise results; however it does NOT meet I6: the fMRI task involves reappraisal and acceptance of sad (negative) images only, and does not include reappraisal of positive emotions nor explicit up- and down-regulation of both positive and negative emotions as required. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (includes healthy control group), I8 (reports within-task regulation contrasts), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I10 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study with a healthy adult sample (I5 and I7 satisfied). However, the fMRI paradigm involves passive/explicit emotion identification and an instrument-count task, not an emotion-regulation reappraisal task (does not meet I6). The paper does not report within-task reappraisal/regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise>look, up/down-regulate>maintain) required by I8. The reported neuroimaging results focus on an mPFC ROI analysis (MarsBaR) rather than presenting a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map; thus it meets exclusion criterion E4 (ROI-only reporting). Therefore the study fails to meet key inclusion criteria (I6, I8, I9) and is excluded.

Exclude: The study does not meet I6 (requires reappraisal tasks involving up-/down-regulation). This work compares mindfulness (Observe) and suppression strategies, not cognitive reappraisal. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I8 (reports within-task contrasts: Suppress>Look, Observe>Look), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates/figures), I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based fMRI study of fear conditioning in healthy adults (meets I5 and I7) but it does NOT investigate emotion regulation via reappraisal (no instructions to up- or down-regulate emotions). The reported within-task contrasts (CS+ > CS−) reflect conditioning, not reappraisal/ regulation contrasts (so I6 and I8 are not met). The target analyses relevant to the review objective (reappraisal contrasts) are absent, and the study therefore does not provide the required whole-brain task-evoked reappraisal maps for inclusion (I9 not met). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I8, I9. Exclusion criteria: none applicable.

The full text reports a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotions (task-based fMRI with reappraisal instructions). Participants were healthy adults with no reported neurological/psychiatric disorders. The paper reports within-task contrasts (regulate > view) and presents group-level whole-brain GLM results (statistical group maps corrected with FDR) alongside ROI analyses. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI emotion regulation studies.

This is a task-based fMRI study that implemented cognitive reappraisal of negative facial expressions (down-regulation). The sample comprises screened healthy adults (N=21 analyzed) with no Axis I diagnoses or psychoactive medication use. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise-Neg vs Maintain-Neg and Maintain-Neg vs Look-Neut) and conducts group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses with reported tables/figures of activations. Results include whole-brain cluster maps and coordinate tables, and ROI extractions were secondary to whole-brain analyses. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Hence the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of task-based fMRI reappraisal studies and is INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain group-level maps, but it does not meet the review’s specific reappraisal criterion (I6). Specifically: (a) Exclusion IDs met: none ([]). (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample with screening), I8 (reports within-task contrasts related to regulation: e.g., exp ng > nt, per ng > nt), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I6 — the cognitive reappraisal manipulation (“reality checking”) was applied only to negative/unknown trials (down-regulation context) and participants were instructed to observe positive/neutral trials; the study does not include reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions nor explicit up- and down-regulation goals as required by I6. Therefore it does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal that includes a healthy control group and reports within-task contrasts and group-level whole-brain maps. Specifically, I5 (task-based fMRI) is satisfied; I7 (includes a healthy adult control group with no psychiatric disorders) is satisfied; I8 (reports a within-task emotion-regulation contrast: Reappraise Negative > Look Negative) and I9 (conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports whole-brain results) and I10 (results reported in text/tables/supplement) are satisfied. However, it does NOT meet I6: the fMRI task involves reappraisal of negative (and neutral) social images using distancing (down-regulation) only; it does not include reappraisal of positive emotions nor explicit up-regulation conditions, so it fails the requirement to include reappraisal of positive and negative emotions and both up- and down-regulation goals. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study must be excluded for not meeting inclusion criterion I6.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain analyses, but it does not investigate cognitive reappraisal (up- or down-regulation of positive/negative emotions). The task manipulates perceived behavioral control over pain and analyzes controllable vs uncontrollable pain, PPI connectivity, and correlations with state anxiety. It does not include an emotion-regulation reappraisal task or within-task contrasts of reappraisal (e.g., “reappraise > look”, “down-regulate > maintain”), so it fails the key inclusion criteria for emotion-regulation reappraisal. Therefore excluded.

Exclusion summary: E4 (only ROI-restricted results for the target emotion-regulation contrast; no accompanying whole-brain group-level voxelwise map for the affect-label vs gender-label contrast). Inclusion met: I5 (task-based fMRI study), I7 (includes a healthy control group), I8 (reports a within-task emotion-regulation contrast: affect label > gender label for HCs). Inclusion not met: I6 (task is affect labeling, an implicit labeling strategy, not cognitive reappraisal with explicit up-/down-regulation goals), I9 (the target emotion-regulation analyses are reported within ROI-constrained searches rather than as group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps; although supplementary whole-brain main effects are mentioned, the critical regulation contrast and group comparisons were ROI-restricted). Full text appears complete. Given the meta-analysis requirement for reappraisal tasks and whole-brain task activation maps, this study does not qualify.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6. The fMRI task uses reappraisal and suppression of negative (and neutral) images only—there is no reappraisal of positive stimuli and no explicit up-regulation condition (only down-regulation of negative affect). It does meet I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample with no psychiatric history), I8 (reports within-task regulation contrasts: Reappraise > Attend, Suppress > Attend), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster FWE correction), and I10 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment of emotion regulation using reappraisal (downregulation) and distraction with positive and negative IAPS stimuli, and includes healthy control groups. It reports within-task contrasts (reappraisal vs view) and group-level analyses. However, the imaging analyses are performed with anatomically defined ROIs (WFU PickAtlas) and thresholded with ROI-based family-wise error correction / small-volume approaches; the paper does not clearly present or describe a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the target healthy control sample. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (only ROI / small-volume-corrected results without an accompanying whole-brain map). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criterion I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise map) is not met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study of emotion regulation in healthy adults that reports a within-task reappraise > look contrast. However, the task only includes reappraisal of negative stimuli (down-regulation) and does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or explicit up-regulation instructions. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (requires reappraisal of positive and negative emotions with up- and down-regulation). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of emotion regulation (reappraisal) in healthy younger and older adults, but the reported target analyses are seed-based psychophysiological interaction (PPI) connectivity contrasts rather than group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. According to the review criteria, studies that report only seed-based connectivity analyses without an accompanying whole-brain task activation map must be excluded (E5). Although the paper refers to neural activity contrasts reported previously (Allard & Kensinger, 2014), the present full text does not provide the required whole-brain task activation maps/voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps for the reported sample. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), and I8 (within-task contrasts related to regulation — PPI contrasts such as reappraisal > passive viewing/selective attention). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (does not include reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions/up- and down-regulation as specified—present analyses focus on down-regulation of negative stimuli), and I9 (no group-level whole-brain task activation maps reported in this paper). Therefore the study must be excluded under E5.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults that reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain group analyses, but it does NOT meet the review's specific reappraisal task requirement (I6). Specifically, while it includes reappraisal variants (Reinterpretation, Detachment), the paradigm only targets downregulation of negative emotions and does not include reappraisal of positive emotions nor explicit up-regulation conditions. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I8 (reports within-task regulation contrasts such as ‘Regulate Negative’ > ‘Permit Negative’), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), and I10 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria are triggered (none of E3–E6 apply). Therefore, because I6 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that explicitly uses cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative affect (Emotion Regulation Task), satisfying the task-based fMRI requirement. It reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (Reappraise > Maintain; Maintain > Look) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and corrected cluster results (tables/figures). The sample includes a combat-exposed control group without PTSD (healthy adult control group) meeting the requirement of at least one healthy adult group. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental materials are not required. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10, and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no sole-ROI-only or connectivity-only reporting, is empirical).

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal in a healthy adult sample and reports whole-brain reappraisal contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look). Specifically, it includes only down-regulation of negative emotions (reappraisal to decrease negative affect). Inclusion criterion I6 requires reappraisal of positive and negative emotions using up- and down-regulation as the regulation goal; this study does not include up-regulation or positive-emotion reappraisal. Therefore I6 is not met and the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that contrasts a cognitive reappraisal “Regulate” condition with a control “Attend” condition and reports group-level whole-brain activation maps. However, the study does not implement the reappraisal manipulation as explicit up- and down-regulation of emotions for positive and negative emotional stimuli as required by I6. The Regulate instruction frames decision context (reducing loss aversion/regret) rather than instructing separate up- and down-regulation of positive and negative emotions. Therefore I6 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of reappraisal (Study 2) and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain group-level results. However it does not meet key inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis: (1) I6 not met — the fMRI task only uses reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotions (no positive-emotion reappraisal and no up-regulation condition); (2) I7 not met — there is no clearly defined healthy adult group free of psychiatric history (the non-DSH participants serve as a depression control group rather than a healthy, no-psychiatric-disorder group); (3) I9 not met for the meta-analysis target (the required target analysis is a group-level whole-brain task map for a healthy adult sample; although whole-brain group comparisons are reported, no healthy-only group whole-brain map is provided). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (reports within-task regulation contrasts), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). Exclusion criteria: none of E3–E6 apply. Therefore the paper is excluded from the current meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that uses cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate anticipatory anxiety (negative emotion). Participants were healthy adults screened for psychiatric disorders. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., regulation vs. anxiety, regulation vs. control) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses (voxelwise one-sample t-tests, coordinates and activations reported). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and not only between-group contrasts).

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion requirements. Specifically, I6 is not met: the task used only negative and neutral stimuli (no positive-emotion reappraisal). I8 and I9 are not met: the paper does not report within-task, group-level whole-brain reappraisal contrasts specifically for the healthy control group (target sample); contrasts are reported across groups and as between-group comparisons. The study does satisfy I5 (task-based fMRI) and I7 (includes a healthy control group). Because the paper effectively reports combined/group-difference results rather than the required healthy-group whole-brain task maps, it falls under exclusion criterion E6 (reports only between-group/interaction-focused results relevant to patient vs control). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults using a standardized mood-induction (happy faces + autobiographical recall). However, it does not implement an explicit cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation paradigm (up- or down-regulation via reappraisal) and does not report within-task reappraisal contrasts such as “reappraise > look”, “down-regulate > maintain”, or equivalent. Analyses are regression-based correlations between MI activation and subjective affect change rather than reappraisal contrasts. Therefore it fails to meet I6 and I8. The manuscript does meet I5, I7, I9 (and acceptable reporting formats per I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive reappraisal in healthy adults and reports the within-task contrast Regulate Negative > Look Negative, with group-level whole-brain results (figures/tables/supplementary). It therefore meets I5, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, it does not satisfy I6: the task involves reappraisal of negative stimuli with down-regulation only and does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or explicit up-regulation conditions. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Thus the study is excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 (requires both positive/negative and up-/down-regulation as specified).

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E4 — the study limited voxelwise analyses to an explicit a priori mask (PFC, ACC, amygdala) rather than reporting a whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation map. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study), I7 (healthy adult sample with no reported neurological/psychiatric disorders), I8 (reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation, e.g., regulation > passive viewing, reappraisal > selective attention). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (does not provide reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions with up- and down-regulation goals; main reported analyses focus on down-regulation of negative affect), I9 (does not report a whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map; analyses were restricted to an a priori mask). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus the paper must be excluded because it reports only ROI/mask-limited voxelwise results without an accompanying whole-brain map required by inclusion criterion I9 and falls under exclusion E4.

The article is a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative affect (Reappraise vs Maintain) in a sample of healthy adults (final N=49). It reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (Reappraise > Maintain), includes whole-brain, group-level activation analyses with voxelwise thresholding and tables/figures, and provides full Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI task study of cognitive reappraisal using negative (aversive) images with healthy adult participants and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I8 (reports within-task reappraisal contrast: Reapp Neg > Look Neg), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I10 (whole-brain results described in text/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 — the task involves only down-regulation of negative emotion (reappraising aversive images); it does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or both up- and down-regulation goals as required. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded solely because it does not satisfy I6.

This is a task-based fMRI study with healthy control participants (I5 and I7 satisfied). However, it does not examine reappraisal as the emotion-regulation strategy required by I6: the study uses attentional distraction versus evaluation, not cognitive reappraisal or explicit up-/down-regulation instructions. Therefore I6 is not met. Additionally, although within-task contrasts of strategy (distraction vs evaluation) are reported, these are not reappraisal contrasts for the target (healthy) sample and the paper does not provide a clear group-level, whole-brain emotion-regulation (reappraisal) contrast for healthy adults as required by I8–I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because it does not meet I6 (reappraisal) and also fails to meet I8 and I9.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: it examines reappraisal only as a down-regulation strategy for negative stimuli (reappraise to decrease negative affect) and does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or both up- and down-regulation goals. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample with screening/exclusions for psychiatric/medical issues), I8 (reports within-task regulation contrasts such as Reappraise > Observe and Label > Observe), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported coordinates and cluster thresholds), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete and contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

Although this study is a task-based fMRI investigation of emotion regulation using reappraisal (negative and positive) in healthy adult participants and reports within-task contrasts (reappraisal > view; distraction > view) with coordinates and figures, the fMRI results were analyzed and reported using anatomically defined ROI-based procedures (WFU PickAtlas) with FWE correction within ROIs. The methods and results do not describe or present a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or whole-brain thresholding/results. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only ROI/SVC results without an accompanying whole-brain map). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I9. Full text appears complete for assessment.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive reappraisal using negative and neutral pictures and reports within-task contrasts (Maintain>Observe; Suppress>Maintain) and whole-brain group-level analyses (supplementary tables referenced). However, it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: the task targets only negative emotion and a down-regulation (suppress/reappraise to decrease) strategy — it does not include positive emotions nor both up- and down-regulation goals. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore, although it satisfies I5, I7, I8, I9 and I10, it fails I6 and must be excluded.

Study is a task-based fMRI investigation of emotion regulation with healthy adult participants and reports group-level whole-brain within-task contrasts (e.g., Target Reappraisal > Appraise) with coordinate tables and FWE-corrected voxelwise results. Thus it meets I5, I7, I8, I9 and I10. However, it does not meet I6: the task involves reappraisal of negative, high-arousal images to down-regulate negative affect (no positive-emotion stimuli and no up-regulation conditions are included). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to satisfy inclusion criterion I6. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of affect labeling in healthy adults that reports within-task contrasts (e.g., label emotion vs match forms; label vs match emotion) and group-level whole-brain GLM maps, and includes a healthy sample (N=45) with appropriate preprocessing and results. Therefore it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I8 (reports within-task emotion-regulation-related contrasts), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I10 (maps/tables described). However, it does NOT meet I6: the meta-analysis requires studies using reappraisal (explicit up- and down-regulation of emotions). This study investigates affect labeling (an incidental/implicit regulation strategy) and centers on effective connectivity (DCM) during labeling rather than explicit reappraisal up-/down-regulation. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Thus, per protocol, the study must be excluded.

This is a longitudinal, task-based fMRI study using an established Emotion Regulation Task (Reappraisal vs Maintain) that instructs participants to down-regulate negative emotion via cognitive reappraisal. Participants were healthy adults with no current/prior psychiatric or neurological disorders. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (Reappraisal vs Maintain) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected thresholds, tables/figures) alongside ROI analyses for the amygdala. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that explicitly tests cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise vs React) across three socio-emotional tasks. It includes a healthy control group with no lifetime psychiatric disorders, reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise > React) for the target HC sample, and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with appropriate multiple-comparison correction (AlphaSim). Results are reported as whole-brain cluster coordinates and figures. The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is complete. This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (I5) that reports within-task contrasts (reappraise-sad > attend-sad) at the group level with voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported in tables/figures (I8, I9, I10) and includes a healthy control group (I7). However, it does NOT meet I6: the fMRI task involves only down-regulation (reappraisal) of negative (sad) images and does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or both up- and down-regulation goals. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to satisfy I6 (required).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal that explicitly instructs healthy adult participants to both decrease and increase emotional responses to previously encoded aversive images. The sample comprises healthy young adults with no reported psychiatric/neurological disorders. The paper reports multiple within-task, group-level contrasts relevant to emotion regulation (e.g., decrease>maintain, increase>maintain, decrease>increase) analyzed with second-level random-effects voxelwise whole-brain analyses (with coordinate tables and figures); a small-volume correction for the amygdala is reported in addition to whole-brain results. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that implemented an explicit reappraisal (mentalizing-reappraisal) task with both up- and down-regulation instructions during gameplay (Dictator Game). The sample is healthy adults screened for psychiatric/medical/neurological illness (n=21). The authors report within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., DOWN > LOOK, UP > LOOK, DOWN+UP > LOOK, and a linear contrast DOWN < LOOK < UP) at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses (cluster-level correction across the whole brain) and present coordinate tables/figures. The paper also reports DCM connectivity analyses, but these are supplemental to whole-brain task activation results. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; includes whole-brain task activation; not resting-state-only; not between-group-only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study does not implement or contrast an instructed reappraisal task. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI with a symptom-provocation task), I7 (includes a healthy control group), and I9 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses for activation decreases). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no fMRI task of instructed up- or down-regulation/reappraisal; participants simply viewed pictures and dispositional reappraisal was measured), and I8 (no within-task emotion-regulation contrast such as “reappraise > look” or “down-regulate > maintain” reported for the target sample). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is ineligible for the meta-analysis focused specifically on task-based reappraisal contrasts.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults and reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts of emotion regulation, but it does NOT meet the review's specific reappraisal criterion (I6). Specifically, the reappraisal manipulation targets down-regulation of a negative autobiographical memory only; it does not include reappraisal of positive emotions nor both up- and down-regulation goals. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I8 (within-task ER contrast reported), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (requires reappraisal of positive and negative emotions using up- and down-regulation). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Consequently the study is excluded for failing I6.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) using cognitive reappraisal to both up- and down-regulate positive and negative emotions (I6). Participants are healthy adults with exclusion of psychiatric/neurological disorders (I7). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation versus experience (e.g., Positive-Regulate > Positive-Experience, Negative-Regulate > Negative-Experience) for the target sample (I8). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain task-evoked maps with cluster-corrected thresholds and peak coordinates reported in tables/figures (I9,I10). No exclusion criteria are met: this is empirical original fMRI data, not ROI-only or connectivity-only, and includes whole-brain task activation results. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion provided).

No exclusion criteria were met. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study), I7 (includes a healthy control group screened for psychiatric/neurological disorders), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses reported), I10 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (task involves reappraisal of negative images with down-regulation only; it does not include reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions nor both up- and down-regulation), I8 (the paper reports task effects across all participants and group contrasts, but does not present a within-task whole-brain contrast specifically for the healthy control group such as reappraise > maintain/look for HC alone). Because not all inclusion criteria are satisfied (notably I6 and I8), the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: None. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI study), I7 (includes a healthy adult control group), I9 (reports group-level whole-brain exploratory analyses/maps), I10 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I6 and I8. The fMRI task is affect labeling of facial expressions (labeling emotion/gender), not cognitive reappraisal involving up-/down-regulation of emotion (e.g., “reappraise > look”, “down-regulate > maintain”). The paper does not report within-task reappraisal contrasts for emotion regulation strategies required by I6/I8. Although it contains task activation and connectivity analyses and healthy controls, it does not test or report reappraisal-based regulation contrasts for the target sample. Full text appears complete.

While this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of healthy adults that reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps (meets I5, I7, I9, I10), it does NOT implement an explicit reappraisal emotion-regulation task (no up-/down-regulation instructions) and does not report within-task contrasts that reflect reappraisal-based regulation (e.g., “reappraise > look”, “down-regulate > maintain”). The task (Cued Emotional Conflict Task) measures cognitive control for emotional information and correlates habitual reappraisal/suppression questionnaire scores with activation, but it does not perform or contrast active reappraisal regulation conditions. Therefore I6 and I8 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed cognitive reappraisal paradigm with explicit downregulation and upregulation conditions for negative emotions. The sample comprises healthy adult participants screened for medical/psychiatric disorders. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (downregulate vs negative look; upregulate vs negative look) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and tables/figures of coordinates. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets the review’s task-based fMRI, reappraisal (up/down) paradigm, healthy sample, within-task contrasts, and whole-brain evidence criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). Note: the study uses negative (and neutral) stimuli rather than positive stimuli; I interpreted I6 as satisfied because the key requirement—reappraisal with up- and down-regulation—is met.

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in a healthy adult sample that used a reappraisal instruction and reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts, it does not meet the meta-analysis’ specific regulation-task requirement (I6). The study’s regulation manipulation (‘Regulate’ vs ‘Attend’) uses perspective-taking reappraisal to reduce loss aversion in financial decisions, primarily targeting down-regulation of negative responses to losses (and not explicitly instructing both up- and down-regulation of positive and negative emotions). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I8 (within-task contrasts of regulation vs attend), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), and I10 (results reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criterion NOT met: I6 (requires reappraisal task involving up- and down-regulation of positive and negative emotions as regulation goals). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level, whole-brain within-task contrasts comparing up- versus down-regulation conditions (IMT > eSUP, eSUP > IMT, IMT > GND, etc.). Thus it meets I5, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, it does NOT meet I6: the study manipulates imitation (IMT) and expressive suppression (eSUP) as up- and down-regulation strategies rather than cognitive reappraisal, and the meta-analysis inclusion requires reappraisal as the emotion-regulation strategy. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study must be excluded from the current meta-analysis because inclusion criterion I6 is not satisfied.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly investigates reappraisal-based emotion regulation using both up- and down-regulation during the Ultimatum Game. Sample: healthy adult participants (n=21) with screening for neurological/psychiatric/medical history. Within-task contrasts related to regulation are reported (e.g., Down + Up > Look; Down < Look < Up; unfair accepted Down > Look; unfair rejected Up > Look), and behavioral effects of up-/down-regulation are shown. Imaging analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results with family-wise error cluster correction; coordinates and statistical tables/figures are provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports within-task, group-level whole-brain contrasts of emotion regulation, it does NOT meet the specific reappraisal task criterion (I6): the reappraisal manipulation involved only down-regulation of negative (unpleasant) pictures and did not include reappraisal of positive emotions or explicit up-regulation targets. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I8 (within-task regulation contrasts: e.g., RU vs CUR / PU vs CUP), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I10 (results reported as whole-brain coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria applied (none of E3–E6 are met). Therefore the study is excluded for failing I6.

This is a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation using cognitive reappraisal in a healthy adult community sample. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I8 (reports within-task contrast for regulation: regulate > look), I9 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I10 (whole-brain results presented with coordinates and figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (requires reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions and use of up- and down-regulation goals). The study only used reappraisal down-regulation of negative stimuli (decrease vs look) and neutral stimuli; it did not include reappraisal of positive emotions or explicit up-regulation conditions. No exclusion criteria were triggered (exclusion_criteria_applied=[]). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) and includes a healthy control group (I7). However it does NOT use an explicit reappraisal paradigm with up-/down-regulation of positive/negative emotions (I6 not met), and it does not report within-task reappraisal contrasts such as “reappraise > look” or “down-regulate > maintain” for the target sample (I8 not met). Additionally, the analyses are ROI-focused (amygdala/insula a priori ROIs and an exploratory ROI mask) rather than providing a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map (I9 not met). Exclusion criterion E4 is therefore met (ROI-only reporting without an accompanying whole-brain map). Summary: Inclusion met: I5, I7. Inclusion NOT met: I6, I8, I9. Exclusion met: E4. Given these failures to meet key inclusion criteria for reappraisal-based whole-brain task contrasts, the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of emotion regulation and reports whole-brain, group-level within-task contrasts (e.g., Sad-Reappraise > Sad-View), but it does NOT meet the review’s specific stimulus/regulation requirement. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (within-task emotion-regulation contrasts reported), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I10 (results reported in tables/figures/text). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (the ER task involved reappraisal of negative/sad stimuli only and focused on down-regulation; it did not include reappraisal of positive emotions nor both up- and down-regulation goals). I7 (target sample) is borderline: participants were non-MDD females with subclinical depressive symptoms and some allowance for dysthymia, so they are not clearly a healthy adult group with no prior psychiatric history as required. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are violated. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it fails to satisfy I6 (and possibly I7).

This is a task-based fMRI experiment of emotion regulation using reappraisal (and distraction) in remitted MDD patients and healthy controls. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal of positive and negative emotional stimuli with regulation goal — here down-regulation), I7 (includes a healthy control group of adults), and I8 (reports within-task regulation contrasts such as reappraisal > view for negative/positive images for the target sample). Exclusion criterion met: E4. The Methods state that anatomically defined ROIs were used to examine activations and thresholding was applied within these ROIs; the reported group comparisons appear to rely on ROI/small-volume approaches and do not present or describe a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map required by I9. Thus the study fails to meet I9 (whole-brain evidence) and is excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).
