Exclusion reasons: E4 (study reports ROI-restricted analyses rather than a group-level whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI with reappraisal and affect-labeling tasks), I7 (healthy adult control sample with no major disorders), I8 (reports within-task regulation contrasts, e.g., Look vs Decrease and Match vs Label). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (reappraisal targeted only negative stimuli and down-regulation, not reappraisal of positive and negative emotions or both up- and down-regulation as specified), I9 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps reported; analyses were ROI-based and PPI restricted to IFG masks). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing the whole-brain reporting requirement (E4) and not meeting I6/I9.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports within-task regulation contrasts and whole-brain group analyses (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10). However, it does not meet I6: the task involves reappraisal of negative and neutral stimuli with down-regulation of negative emotion only; it does not include positive emotions nor explicit up-regulation as required by I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that includes a healthy young adult group (I7), reports within-task reappraisal contrasts (decrease negative > look negative) (I8), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation results (I9/I10). However, it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: the task involves down-regulation of negative emotions (reappraisal of negative stimuli) only and does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or up-regulation trials. Therefore it fails to satisfy all required inclusion criteria and must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that uses reappraisal (distancing) and reports within-task regulation contrasts and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results. However, the study applies reappraisal to positive emotion (anticipation of monetary reward) and implements down-regulation only; it does not include reappraisal of negative emotions nor both up- and down-regulation goals as required by inclusion criterion I6. Therefore it fails to meet I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion based on unmet inclusion criterion I6: the task involves distancing reappraisal to down-regulate anticipatory anxiety (negative emotion) only; it does not include reappraisal of positive emotions nor explicit up-regulation goals. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study using BOLD fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample with no reported neurological/psychiatric disorders), I8 (reports within-task reappraisal contrasts, e.g., R–NR), I9 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed), I10 (whole-brain results and coordinates reported in text/tables/figures). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6 apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. However, the experimental task examines decision-induced attitude change/cognitive dissonance (choice between similarly rated items) and does not implement an explicit emotion regulation reappraisal paradigm (no instructions to reappraise/up- or down-regulate emotions). The paper does not report within-task emotion-regulation contrasts (e.g., “reappraise > look”, “down-regulate > maintain”, “up-regulate > maintain”) for the target sample. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 (task: reappraisal of emotions as emotion regulation strategy) and I8 (reports within-task emotion-regulation contrasts). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of emotion regulation comparing reappraisal and distraction in healthy adults and reports whole-brain group-level contrasts (e.g., reappraisal emotional vs. view emotional) with tables and figures. However, Inclusion Criterion I6 appears unmet: the meta-analysis requires reappraisal using up- and down-regulation goals, whereas this study implements reappraisal only as down-regulation (decrease emotional intensity) and does not include an up-regulation reappraisal condition. All other inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet I6 (missing up-regulation condition).

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI experiment directly testing emotion regulation via cognitive reappraisal (REAP) and expressive suppression (ESUP) across positive and negative visual scenes. Participants were healthy adult volunteers (19 right-handed women) with no reported neurological/psychiatric disorders. The paper presents within-task, group-level whole-brain (random-effects SPM) contrasts related to regulation (e.g., REAP>ESUP, REAP>NAT, ESUP>REAP) with voxelwise thresholds and tables of peak coordinates. Analyses and results are clearly described at the whole-brain level (including RFX maps, cluster thresholds, and coordinate tables), meeting the review’s reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, empirical fMRI data in healthy adults). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal paradigm with positive, negative and neutral IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts of interest (e.g., Reappraise > Experience and Experience > Reappraise), performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and provides coordinates/tables/figures, and uses a healthy adult sample screened for neurological/psychiatric disorders. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI reappraisal study with up- and down-regulation of emotional responses, healthy control group, within-task contrasts, and whole-brain group-level analyses are reported. However, the study uses negative and neutral stimuli only (no positive emotion stimuli), and thus does not meet inclusion criterion I6 which requires reappraisal of positive and negative emotions. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that reports a within-task emotion-regulation contrast (affect label vs affect match) (I8) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (I9) with tables/figures (I10). However, it does not use an explicit cognitive reappraisal paradigm (I6) — the regulation manipulation is affect labeling (incidental labeling/‘putting feelings into words’), not up-/down-regulation via reappraisal. Therefore it fails the specific reappraisal task requirement (I6) and must be excluded. Note: control participants are described as healthy volunteers (but some had lifetime substance/mood histories), so the strict ‘no prior report’ criterion for healthy samples (I7) is also not clearly met, providing an additional concern. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly met.

Decision: EXCLUDE because the study does not meet I6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI using ASL perfusion during an emotion regulation task), I7 (includes a group of non-anxious/healthy elderly comparison subjects), I8 (reports within-task contrasts related to regulation: worry suppression > rest and worry induction > rest for the healthy control group), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported using SPM with FDR correction), I10 (whole-brain results presented in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (the task is personalized worry induction and suppression, i.e., suppression/avoidance, not an explicit reappraisal paradigm of up- and down-regulation of positive/negative emotions). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) . Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that trained participants in cognitive reappraisal and used an in-scanner emotion regulation task (Reduce vs. Maintain). The task specifically implements reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotion (Reduce>Maintain) and reports within-task contrasts at the group level. The paper includes whole-brain, voxelwise analyses corrected for multiple comparisons and reports significant clusters/tables and figures. The sample includes a healthy control group (Normal Anxiety) screened to have no history of anxiety or mood disorders, meeting the target-sample requirement. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Full article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present, so the full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that uses cognitive reappraisal as an emotion regulation strategy (down-regulation of negative emotion) during an event-related fMRI encoding task. Participants were healthy adults with no reported neurological/psychiatric disorders. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., reappraise > view, reappraise > suppress) at the group level using whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with cluster correction (FLAME, Z>2.3, cluster P<0.05). Results (figures/tables) present whole-brain activation and coordinates. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion decision: No exclusion criteria were triggered. Inclusion/exclusion summary: This is a task-based fMRI study (I5 met) that reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses and tabulated/figure results (I9 and I10 met). However, it does NOT manipulate emotion regulation via instructed reappraisal/up- or down-regulation (it used an emotion-word Stroop task), so I6 is not met. The sample was recruited partly from an outpatient mental-health clinic and is not clearly described as a group of healthy adults with no history of neurological/psychiatric disorders, so I7 is not met. The paper does not report within-task reappraisal contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look), so I8 is not met. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied, the study is excluded.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level whole-brain results and coordinates (I5, I7, I9, I10 met), the task did NOT instruct participants to perform reappraisal/up- or down-regulation of emotions. Emotion-regulation was assessed as a trait (ERQ) and analyses correlated habitual strategy scores with passive expectation/presentation contrasts (e.g., EXP neg > neut). The study does not include within-task instructed reappraisal contrasts such as “reappraise > look” or explicit up-/down-regulation conditions (I6 and I8 are not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the paper does not meet all inclusion criteria required for this meta-analysis and is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal in healthy adults that reports within-task contrasts (increase > maintain, decrease > maintain) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (FWE-corrected clusters and coordinate tables). However, it only used negative and neutral stimuli (no positive emotions), so it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I6, which requires reappraisal of positive and negative emotions. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Exclusion criteria applied: none (E#: none).

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of reappraisal with healthy adults and reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., distance > look, interaction effects) using SPM2, it tests only a distancing (reappraisal) down-regulation strategy applied to negative interpersonal images. It does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or any up-regulation conditions. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 which requires reappraisal of positive and negative emotions using up- and down-regulation goals. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a reappraisal paradigm with clear within-task contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample with no reported psychiatric/neurological disorders), I8 (reports within-task emotion-regulation contrast: Reappraise > Negative), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps with FDR correction), I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (study only examined reappraisal of negative stimuli with down-regulation; it did not include reappraisal of positive emotions or up-regulation conditions as required by I6). No exclusion criteria were triggered (no E3–E6). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I6 (requires reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions and up- and/or down-regulation).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s emotion-regulation task requirements. Specifically, the fMRI task involved passive viewing and affect ratings of partners' facial expressions with no instructions to reappraise or to up-/down-regulate emotion, and the reported contrasts are stimulus valence contrasts (e.g., partner negative > partner neutral) rather than within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look or down-regulate > maintain). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I9 (group-level whole-brain/random-effects activation reported), and I10 (results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (task is not a reappraisal up-/down-regulation paradigm) and I8 (no within-task emotion-regulation contrast reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look) and provides tables/figures of results. However, the reappraisal manipulation involves only down-regulation of negative emotion (negative pictures) and does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or any up-regulation instructions. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I6 (requires reappraisal of positive and negative emotions using up- and down-regulation). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I8 (within-task regulation contrasts reported), I9 (group-level whole-brain analyses), I10 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of script-driven imagery in BPD patients and healthy controls, but it does NOT investigate emotion regulation via explicit reappraisal instructions (no up-/down-regulation goal) and does not report within-task reappraisal contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look; down-regulate > maintain). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (includes a healthy control group without psychiatric disorders), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I10 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (task is not a reappraisal paradigm of positive/negative emotions with up-/down-regulation goals) and I8 (no within-task emotion-regulation contrasts reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus the study is excluded for failing I6 and I8.

This is a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation that reports a within-task contrast for reappraisal (high-control/reappraise > low-control/rate) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (coordinates reported). Participants are healthy adults. However, the emotion task involves down-regulation of negative emotional faces only; it does not include reappraisal of positive emotions nor explicit up-regulation of emotion. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (requires reappraisal of positive and negative emotions and use of up- and down-regulation goals). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly tests emotion regulation strategies while participants recall negative autobiographical memories. It explicitly frames the “analyze” condition as a memory-analog of cognitive reappraisal and includes up- (feel) and down-regulation (accept, analyze) of negative affect. The sample consists of screened healthy adult participants with exclusions for current treatment/medication, and analyses report within-task, group-level voxelwise contrasts (e.g., feel vs accept, analyze vs feel) using whole-brain random-effects GLM with tables/figures of activations and cluster-corrected thresholds. Full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the study does not meet key inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI: BOLD fMRI perceptual face-processing task), I7 (healthy adult sample: 56 healthy female adults), I9 (reports group-level whole-brain regression analyses relating ERQ scores to task activation), and I10 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (the task does not involve an instructed reappraisal paradigm or up-/down-regulation instructions; the study assesses individual differences in spontaneous reappraisal use rather than an explicit reappraisal task), and I8 (no within-task regulation contrast such as “reappraise > look” or “down-regulate > maintain” is reported for the target sample; primary contrast is faces > shapes and correlations with trait scores). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of instructed cognitive reappraisal in healthy adults that reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., decrease negative > look negative) and group-level whole-brain activation maps/tables. However, it only examines down-regulation of negative emotions and does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or any up-regulation conditions. Thus it fails inclusion criterion I6 (requires reappraisal of positive and negative emotions using up- and down-regulation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion.

This task-based fMRI study recruited healthy adult participants, used reappraisal and suppression tasks, reported within-task contrasts (reappraise > watch, suppress > watch), and conducted group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates/tables. However it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: the review requires reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions and use of up- and down-regulation goals; this study examines only reappraisal (and suppression) of negative (disgust) stimuli with down-regulation. No exclusion criteria were met. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it reports only seed-based task-dependent connectivity (PPI) analyses and does not present a group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the emotion regulation contrasts. Exclusion ID E5 applies. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I8 (within-task contrast related to emotion regulation: Reappraise > Maintain). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (study only examines down-regulation of negative emotions, not reappraisal of both positive and negative or both up- and down-regulation), I9 (does not report a whole-brain task-evoked activation map in this paper; main activation results are referenced from a prior publication). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper must be excluded per E5.

This is a task-based fMRI study that uses an emotion reappraisal paradigm with up- (increase) and down- (decrease) regulation instructions for positive and negative IAPS images. It includes a healthy control group with no reported psychiatric disorders and reports within-task contrasts (decrease > attend) for the control sample. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise mixed-effects GLMs with normalization, smoothing, and cluster-size correction; results are reported as voxelwise maps and clusters/coordinates. All specified inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present; supplemental materials are referenced but not required for eligibility.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts of an instructed cognitive control ("reality checking") condition versus a basic/no-control condition and within-group contrasts (negative>neutral, unknown>neutral) (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10). However it does not satisfy I6: the task did not explicitly implement reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions with instructions for both up- and down-regulation. The cognitive strategy was applied primarily to down-regulate anticipatory negative/unknown emotion and there was no explicit up-regulation instruction or balanced reappraisal paradigm for positive emotions. Therefore the study fails the I6 inclusion criterion and must be excluded.

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study that trains participants to reappraise emotional images and explicitly uses up- (increase/enhance) and down- (decrease/suppress) regulation instructions for negative affect. Sample consists of healthy adults (no neurological illness reported). The paper reports within-task contrasts (increase vs. attend; decrease vs. attend) and a whole-brain voxelwise ANOVA with corrected cluster results and coordinate tables/figures at the group level. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based reappraisal fMRI and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that used cognitive reappraisal instructions to both up- and down-regulate emotional responses to threat-related (negative) pictures. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=24 females) with no reported neurological/psychiatric disorders. The paper reports within-task contrasts of emotion regulation (increase-minus-view, decrease-minus-view, view-minus-decrease) computed at the group level using random-effects analysis. Whole-brain results are reported (whole-brain analyses with corrected thresholds and tables/figures), in addition to ROI analyses. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (non-empirical, ROI-only without whole-brain map, connectivity/resting-only, or only between-group contrasts) are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study in a healthy adult sample that reports group-level whole-brain analyses and coordinates. However, the experimental paradigm involves observing and labeling emotional faces (observe only; emotion-label vs gender-label) rather than an explicit reappraisal task with up- or down-regulation instructions. Therefore it does not meet I6 (reappraisal of positive/negative emotions using up- and down-regulation) and does not provide the within-task reappraisal contrasts required by I8 (e.g., reappraise > look, down-regulate > maintain). I5, I7, I9, and I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and within-task contrasts showing cognitive distraction modulates anticipatory emotion. However, it does not investigate reappraisal as an emotion-regulation strategy (no up- or down-regulation via reappraisal of positive/negative emotions); instead it manipulates cognitive load (distraction). Inclusion criterion I6 (reappraisal task using up-/down-regulation) is not met, so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (self-distraction > no self-distraction) and group-level voxelwise results. However, it does NOT investigate reappraisal of positive and negative emotions using up- and down-regulation as the regulation goal (it studies thought suppression/self-distraction during anticipatory anxiety rather than reappraisal up-/down-regulation of emotions). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 and must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult women that reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Don't Think > Think; Think Negative > Think Neutral) and ROI analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I8 (reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation/suppression), I9 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), and I10 (whole-brain results reported via coordinates and figures). However, it fails the critical inclusion criterion I6: the experimental paradigm examines thought suppression (think vs. don’t think) rather than reappraisal-based emotion regulation (up- or down-regulation via reappraisal). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded because it does not use reappraisal as the emotion regulation strategy required by I6.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that uses reappraisal and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses, it does not report an explicit within-task regulation contrast (e.g., REAPPRAISE > NAT/LOOK or down-regulate > maintain) in the full text provided. The paper focuses on parametric regressions of social vs nonsocial content within each viewing condition and on attachment-related modulation; main whole-brain contrasts comparing regulation conditions (REAP > NAT or REAP > ESUP) are said to be reported in a separate paper. Therefore Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I9 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (the paper uses reappraisal to down-regulate but does not clearly present reappraisal contrasts framed as up- and down-regulation goals across conditions), I8 (no explicit within-task regulation contrast such as REAP > NAT is reported in this full text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that examines cognitive reappraisal and reports whole-brain group-level task contrasts, it does not meet inclusion criterion I6. Specifically, the task involves reappraisal aimed at down-regulating negative self-beliefs only (react vs reappraise of negative self-beliefs). The inclusion criteria require reappraisal of positive and negative emotions and use of up- and down-regulation goals. The study satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (includes a healthy control group), I8 (reports within-task contrasts related to reappraisal), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), and I10 (results reported in text/tables/figures). It fails I6 (no positive-emotion reappraisal or up-regulation condition). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED for not meeting I6.
